title: Microtutorials + Playground Roadmap (v1) - draft
content:
Overview:

This is an early roadmap/draft for a set of focused, 3–7 minute "microtutorials" combined with an embedded online Playground (interactive REPL + examples) to reduce time-to-first-success for SDK consumers. Goal is to ship a low-friction learning surface for engineers evaluating or integrating Redwood SDKs into real apps.

Why microtutorials + Playground?
- Short, task-oriented lessons beat long monolithic quickstarts for discoverability and completion.
- Live playgrounds let users run real requests without setup friction (sanboxed keys, ephemeral tokens).
- Combine text + runnable snippets + observability hooks so we can measure success and iterate fast.

Top goals (measurable):
- Reduce median time-to-first-success from sign-up to a valid request by 40% in first 90 days.
- Increase completion rate of first microtutorial to 60% for new SDK signups.
- Surface 3 high-impact friction points via telemetry (auth errors, network, misunderstanding of streaming).

Primary audience:
- Software engineers evaluating Redwood for a POC.
- Product engineers implementing an initial chat or generation feature.
- Platform/infra engineers validating deployment patterns (Dedicated/Private later).

Planned artifacts (MVP scope):
1) 6 microtutorials (each 3–7 min):
   - Quick auth + first request (curl + JS + Python)
   - Streaming responses: show partial tokens + cancellation
   - Embeddings: quick vector create and search example
   - Batching & cost-control: how to set a batch policy + telemetry
   - Error handling & fallbacks: model variant fallback example
   - Running locally against a private endpoint (VPC/on-prem primer)
2) Playground: web-based REPL that can run the JS/Python snippets, switch models, toggle streaming, and show per-request token/latency breakdown.
3) Microtutorial template: standard header, prerequisites, 2–3 steps, expected output, quick debugging tips, telemetry checkpoints.
4) Instrumentation plan: events to track (tutorial_start, tutorial_complete, snippet_run, snippet_error, playground_token_request).

Microtutorial format (template):
- Title (clear success metric)
- Audience + estimated time
- Pre-reqs (1–2 lines)
- 3 steps (copyable snippets)
- Expected output + where to look in Console (cost/latency)
- Quick troubleshooting (top 3 failures)
- Next steps (links to deeper docs)

Example microtutorial (draft):
Title: "Streaming a Chat Response in under 5 minutes"
Audience: Engineers adding a low-latency chat feature
Time: 5m
Pre-reqs: API key in Console (can use ephemeral Playground key)
Steps:
1) Install: npm i @redwood/inference (or pip install redwood-inference)
2) Minimal JS example:

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the last meeting notes' }] });
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta);
}
```

Expected output: progressive tokens printed; Console shows latency breakdown and token count.
Troubleshooting: 401 -> check key; stalled stream -> check network/region; partial output -> model timed out -> retry with fallback.
Telemetry checkpoints: snippet_run, streaming_started, streaming_complete, streaming_error.

Playground details (MVP):
- Embedded code editor with Run button and quick toggles: model, temperature, streaming on/off.
- Two sandbox modes: (a) ephemeral key (no account), (b) linked account (persist).
- A lightweight stub backend that proxies requests to Redwood with rate-limits and usage caps.
- Show token/latency breakdown per run inline, with option to open the request trace in Console if user has access.

Instrumentation plan (events and KPIs):
- Events: tutorial_shown, tutorial_clicked, tutorial_start, snippet_run, snippet_error, playground_run, playground_error, tutorial_complete.
- KPIs: tutorial_completion_rate, median_time_to_first_run, playground_run_success_rate, percent_users_opening_console_from_tutorial.
- Sampling: capture detailed telemetry for first 10k tutorial runs, then sample 1/10 thereafter.

UX experiments (early ideas):
- A/B: full page tutorial vs inline microtutorial in the Console route. Measure completion and retention.
- Nudges: Show a "Run in Playground" CTA on model catalog pages for beginner-friendly models.
- Pre-auth experiment: allow a 3-run anonymous sandbox to reduce friction.

Implementation milestones (quarterly):
- Week 0–3: finalize templates + author first 3 microtutorials + mockups for Playground (owner: Asha)
- Week 4–7: Playground alpha (internal) + telemetry plumbing + integrate 3 microtutorials (owner: Jordan)
- Week 8–12: Public beta + instrumented metrics + feedback collection (owner: Diego)
- Week 13–16: Iterate on tutorials, add 3 more, ship small Console CTA (owner: Priya)

Open questions / risks:
- Security: how do we safely provision ephemeral keys for anonymous sandbox without billing abuse? (Ops/Policy to weigh in)
- Cost: playground runs will incur tokens — need quota/cost gating and clear UX about limits.
- Scope creep: don't try to replicate full Console; focus on first-request success and measurable completion.

TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Create Confluence spec for Playground auth flow (assignee: Priya)
- [ ] Draft five minimal microtutorials and get SME review (assignee: Asha)
- [ ] Spike on proxy infra cost estimates and abuse mitigation (assignee: Jordan)
- [ ] Wire basic telemetry events into analytics pipeline (assignee: Diego)

Notes to reviewers:
- Prefer pragmatic scope for Q1. We can always iterate on more advanced interactive features after we validate the conversion/engagement signal.
- Look for missing edge-case tutorials (e.g., long-context usage, dedicated capacity binding).
- If you want to demo an end-to-end experience, contact me and I can provision a dev sandbox.

Related tickets / links:
- ENG-1024: Playground infra spike (linked)
- GH: redwood-inference/redwood-sdk PR #482 (playground-client)
- Slack thread: #devx-playground (search for "playground alpha")

Rough timeline for copy + authoring: plan to draft first 3 microtutorials within two weeks of sign-off and aim to get internal trials by Week 6.

Draft done by: Asha Patel (eng-developer-experience)
Feedback welcome — ping in #devx-playground or add inline comments in Confluence.
